channel.title: Signal & Noise Private
channel.description: Signal & Noise is a personal podcast made for Augusto Restrepo. Each episode takes a topic he's been following — articles, posts, research and conversations he curates from across the web — and double-clicks on it. Max, the optimist, makes the bull case; Lena, the skeptic, pokes holes in it. Together they separate the signal from the noise, so the big ideas are easier to understand and judge. Casual, curious, and grounded in facts.

item.title: NAUT: Can You Read Your Way to a 10x? — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) dig into Nautilus Biotechnology (NAUT), the Seattle proteomics company the 10am.pro group has been debating as the "read" layer of the biology-is-code thesis, on a day the stock jumped about 30% with no company news we could find. They cover what proteoforms are and why they matter, the September Nature Methods tau paper, the July pivot from Broadscale to proteoform assays (tau first, then AKT1 in oncology, roughly 20 assays targeted by mid-2028), and the money: about $130M in cash, roughly $14M of quarterly burn, a raise expected before mid-2027 and a new $125M at-the-market program. They also run NAUT through the lessons from Lucas's LLM 10x stock contest and his "Linares lens" chart. A made-up guest, Bev (a fictional retired lab-instrument saleswoman), asks who actually buys a roughly $1M machine.
Sources: the 10am.pro group discussion; Lucas's LLM 10x Stock Contest PDFs and Linares-lens chart; the proteomics paper shared in the group (Cell Reports Medicine spotlight on a Nature Medicine plasma-proteome aging-clock study); Hernán's "Biology is Code" page (mercados.10am.pro/biology-is-code); Antonio Linares, "Nautilus: Tesla for Proteomics" (Sep 28, 2026); Nautilus Q2 2026 results and earnings call, the Sep 4 Nature Methods release and the Sep 11 8-K; prices as of mid-afternoon Sep 29, 2026. Numbers are rounded, and company claims are flagged as such. Bev is fictional. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Thirty percent before lunch; 2. Why proteins, why now; 3. The pivot nobody clapped for; 4. Bev sells the machine; 5. Cash, burn, and the at-the-market button; 6. Through Lucas's lenses; 7. Revolution, option, or lottery ticket.

item.title: Biology Eats the Market — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) debate Antonio Linares's "bio/acc basket": his claim that biology drives most market returns over the next decade, and his four picks. Nautilus (NAUT) reads the proteome, Recursion (RXRX) designs drugs with A.I., ImmunityBio (IBRX) reboots the immune system with Anktiva, and MiNK Therapeutics (INKT) takes iNKT cell therapy after solid tumors. Max makes the case from the post and its 33-minute video: biology becomes code, a read, design, reboot and strike stack, disciplined management teams, and pharma money already flowing into Recursion. Lena pushes back with the latest filings: Nautilus's first revenue of about $0.2M and its Broadscale delay, Recursion's cash burn, ImmunityBio's 45x sales valuation and the FDA warning letter, and MiNK's roughly $9M cash plus a 17-patient phase 2 with zero responses. A made-up guest, Nigel, drops by to heckle the whole idea of "platform" biotech.
Source (credit): Antonio Linares (@alc2022) on X, Sep 28, 2026, https://x.com/alc2022/status/2104620231922745534 (post and attached video). Also referenced: Q2 2026 results and filings from Nautilus, Recursion, ImmunityBio and MiNK; ImmunityBio's FDA warning letter and PDUFA date; MiNK's AACR 2026 phase 2 poster; market prices as of the Sep 28, 2026 close. Numbers are rounded. The hosts flag claims they couldn't verify on air. Nigel is fictional. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. Biology is the new compute; 2. Read it, then design it; 3. Reboot and strike; 4. A stack or four lottery tickets?.

item.title: HIMS Isn't Telemedicine — Max vs Lena (Special)
item.description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) talk through "HIMS No Es Telemedicina", a Substack piece by Hernán Jaramillo and Antonio Linares of 10ampro. The piece argues that the market prices HIMS like a call center that hands out prescriptions, and that this is a category error. Its case rests on Linares's "closed loop" idea, with Spotify and Duolingo as comparisons: intake, treatment, follow-up and outcome, all owned by one company. Lena pushes back on the customer-service horror story, the FTC case (including the health-data sharing allegations the article leaves out), acquired versus organic growth, competition from Novo, Amazon and OpenAI, and the empty "sold with margin" box: negative free cash flow and a shrinking gross margin.
Source article (credit): Hernán Jaramillo & Antonio Linares, "HIMS No Es Telemedicina", 10ampro on Substack, Sep 27, 2026, https://substack.com/home/post/p-217692613. The framework comes from Antonio Linares's "The State of the Ontology Velocity" (Sep 15, 2026). Also referenced: the Hims & Hers Q2 2026 results and earnings call (Aug 10, 2026), the FTC complaint and press release (Jul 29, 2026), Teladoc's Q2 2026 results, and public HIMS price data as of the Sep 25, 2026 close. Numbers are rounded. Claims the hosts couldn't verify are flagged on air. This is not investment advice.
Chapters: 1. The double charge; 2. Loop, not data; 3. Teladoc's graveyard and the four links; 4. The FTC and the anecdote; 5. Who copies it, and the empty box.
